title: Time and days
topic: telling time; days of the week (יוֹם רִאשׁוֹן…); Shabbat
why: Days numbered starting from Sunday, the Israeli weekend, and telling time with the numbers you already know. With יֵשׁ לִי זְמַן, you can now set up a meeting.

{"lessons": ["

The days: first, second…

In Hebrew, the days of the week have no names: they're numbered starting from Sunday, with יוֹם (day) followed by an ordinal number. Only Saturday has a real name: שַׁבָּת.

DayHebrewPronunciationWord for word
Sundayיוֹם רִאשׁוֹןyom rishonfirst day
Mondayיוֹם שֵׁנִיyom shenisecond day
Tuesdayיוֹם שְׁלִישִׁיyom shlishithird day
Wednesdayיוֹם רְבִיעִיyom revi'ifourth day
Thursdayיוֹם חֲמִישִׁיyom khamishififth day
Fridayיוֹם שִׁשִּׁיyom shishisixth day
SaturdayשַׁבָּתshabatShabbat

The Israeli weekend (סוֹף שָׁבוּעַ, \"end of week\") is Friday and Saturday; יוֹם רִאשׁוֹן (Sunday) is a working day: many people work מִיּוֹם רִאשׁוֹן עַד יוֹם חֲמִישִׁי (from Sunday to Thursday; עַד, ad = until). On Friday evening, many families have dinner together, and people wish each other שַׁבָּת שָׁלוֹם.

\"On Monday,\" \"on Mondays\": בְּיוֹם שֵׁנִי (be-yom sheni). To ask what day it is: אֵיזֶה יוֹם הַיּוֹם? — הַיּוֹם יוֹם שְׁלִישִׁי. (Today is Tuesday.)

", "

What time is it?

מָה הַשָּׁעָה? (ma ha-sha'a?), word for word \"what the hour?\" You answer הַשָּׁעָה + the number, with no verb \"to be.\" The word שָׁעָה (hour) is feminine, so you use the counting forms you already know.

הַשָּׁעָה שָׁלוֹשׁ.It's three o'clock. [ha-sha'a shalosh]
HebrewPronunciationTime
הַשָּׁעָה שָׁלוֹשׁ וְעֶשֶׂרha-sha'a shalosh ve-eser3:10
הַשָּׁעָה שָׁלוֹשׁ וָרֶבַעha-sha'a shalosh va-reva3:15
הַשָּׁעָה שָׁלוֹשׁ וָחֵצִיha-sha'a shalosh va-khetsi3:30
הַשָּׁעָה רֶבַע לְאַרְבַּעha-sha'a reva le-arba3:45 (\"a quarter to four\")

\"At three o'clock\": בְּשָׁלוֹשׁ (be-shalosh), with בְּ attached to the number. In speech, people count from 1 to 12 and add the time of day: עֶשֶׂר בַּלַּיְלָה (ten in the evening).

In וָחֵצִי and וָרֶבַע, \"and\" is written with an a: va-khetsi, va-reva. You'll also hear ve-khetsi.

", "

Morning, noon, evening and night

HebrewPronunciationMeaning
בֹּקֶרbokermorning
צָהֳרַיִםtsohorayimnoon, early afternoon
עֶרֶבerevevening
לַיְלָהlaylanight

\"In the morning,\" \"in the evening\": the article and בְּ merge into בַּ or בָּ. Learn these four expressions as they are: בַּבֹּקֶר, בַּצָּהֳרַיִם, בָּעֶרֶב, בַּלַּיְלָה.

אֲנִי קָם בְּשֶׁבַע בַּבֹּקֶר.I get up at seven in the morning. [ani kam be-sheva ba-boker]

In צָהֳרַיִם, the vowel under ה (a hataf kamats) is read o: tso-ho-ra-yim. And for greetings: בֹּקֶר טוֹב (good morning), עֶרֶב טוֹב (good evening), לַיְלָה טוֹב (good night).
